comment: A few reroutes along the way, but a great little hike!

The hike was wonderful! The forest was beautiful, and the trail had a nice variety of scenery and terrain. The view of Inglis Falls was absolutely gorgeous and well worth the walk. I would definitely recommend this place!
Lots of little side trails yo get off course.
Nice trail, well marked. Some uphill and downhill but nothing too hard. The view of the Inglis falls are amazing. Worth the trip from that.
I didn't think it was worth the money
Really well signed hike with lots of options to do little detours and add ins. Definitely need good footwear
Very nice trail, but the falls was covered by a dam and a parking lot, and the trail ended at the top of the falls with no good viewpoint.
Great!
Hiked this trail Oct 18th. Absolutely stunning in the autumn. Kind of busy, but I didn’t expect anything less! It’s such a beauty of a trail.
Some difficult places, but overall doable. Beautiful views,  specially at the Falls.
Incline is hard on this one
Great rocks and variety of terrain
Saw the salmon running. Amazing.
Great trail!
really nice trail, especially walking from Harrison Park Campground!

Some steep parts, but starts on a paved bike trail, goes towards the falls and is very beautiful! It’s definitely worth seeing and I managed to get it done in 90min, so not too long either! There are some boardwalks, and right by the falls is a washroom. I didn’t have to pay parking at the campground, although not sure if I should have.
Definitely use All Trail. Easy to get turned around.
Parked at the Arboretum for free and took the beautiful connecting trails to the falls and back, many cool mushrooms and rock formations.
Great mix of terrain, great veiws of the river along the way! Completed with a one year old so lots of exploring!

Stick to the right of the forest at the beginning as it’s much nicer than the paved path. You walk along a running river.
Once at the top of the waterfall walk another 200m and take the little board walk/stairs for a nice view.
Enjoyed this trail.
Beautiful, easy to get to.  Would love to return.

Very nice trail. I would say moderate if you go off trail which I did and got lost there is a lot of up and down but if you stick to trail you will be fine. It was a very nice walk for me and my pup. Bring proper footwear. A ran into a couple with flip flops who also got lost and it was a bit scary for them in sections. Beautiful waterfalls that cascade for a picture right by the parking lot. 10 dollars to park at the falls or go to Harrison park for free and hike up.
Really great hike! Quite hilly, great terrain changes. Park at Harrison park, it’s free and u walk towards the falls. Sorta muddy, but came after a rainy day.
Early morning walk, nice & quiet trail with a gorgeous water fall to cap it all!

The Inglis map indicates a turn off flagged in purple however it is actually in light blue. We kissed the turn off and continued on the Bruce trail. It was still a nice hike, and when we eventually backtracked to the turn off it was equally nice!
nice lengthy hike, great views and scenery. Well worth to visit
Trail is in good condition. Bugs are starting to make an appearance.
Beginning was paved but quickly became a dirt trail. We didn't follow the trail exactly, signage was a bit unclear, but all the paths met up eventually so it worked out. The falls were beautiful!!
Amazing views from the top of Inglis waterfall cap off an amazing trail system!

Geology hike .   Very interesting.
Learned many things about rocks, formation, time line and plant names
Beautiful trail rugged at times with some steep climbs
Very nice on a cold day after a fresh snowfall.
Beautiful hike. Poles for winter conditions on steep and rocky sections were beneficial.
Beautiful scenic hike along the river

parked at Harrison Park as its free (vs at Inglis Falls) and did the hike to Inglis Falls and back, totaled to 1h45min. First quarter of the trail is paved/flat gravel however majority is through the forest with rocks and 2 portions of harder level climbs. Overall diverse route with good scenery including bridges, wooden crossways, and of course the Inglis Falls. Would recommend hiking shoes due to uneven ground.
Very few wet places; Inglis Falls section is quiet, Harrison Park busier but overall quiet and a beautiful fall hike.
Glorious!!
Waayyy too many peeps

Lovely view of the colourful autumn trees. We got to see salmon swimming up the river - very cool! The dogs loved it. some parts are fairly steep with tree roots and rocks on the trail, so it may be quite difficult for the elderly, small children, and those with physical disabilities.
CAD 10 for parking, the park at the other end is beautiful. Better toilet at the other end as well.
Nice trail that was easy to follow.  We did the short loop.
Great hike for watching the salmon run and not very busy! Hiked easily in crocs and a dog in tow.
Great hike with views of the salmon swimming upstream.
Great trail lots of cool rock formations and a good hike overall
It was beautiful but not “easy” lots of uphill but it’s fun!
If you go before noon the trail is not very busy. We loved the hike!
Watch out for confusing side trails...destination signage is limited
When I went trail to bottom was closed.  View from top was nice.
Parking at the park is free. The prettiest waterfall ever. Large paved section. Very chill and easy hike.
Great well maintained trail. Lots of roots and rocks so mind your step. Follows a river so some good opportunities to stop and contemplate.
Lots of cool unique features. The path at times was very rooty and uphill
Moderate trail with some difficulty (steep inclines)in great condition. Nice views of the falls
Had a fun hike with my family on a gorgeous Sunday afternoon. While there were some muddy parts, overall, this was a very good hike.

Well travelled trail.  A few rocky inclines from 
 Harrison Park to Inglis Falls but the  Falls at the end is totally worth it.

A little muddy in a few low lying spots.  Washroom facilities available at both ends of the trail.

Easy trail from Harrison Park to Inglis Falls!
Lots of free parking at Harrison park and many things to see and do - take out booth, sit down restaurant and washrooms. 
The trail meanders along the river for a good portion of the trail creating a beautiful atmosphere - and a few spots for the dogs to cool down!
There are some moderately challenging spots with some incline/decline but for the most part the trail is flat and easy.  The section closest to Harrison Park is  a paved walking trail before heading into the forest.  
Lots of shade with gorgeous tree canopy - trees are tall and towering. 
Inglis falls is obviously the show stopper - and lots of trails to explore if you have the time and energy before looping back to the park. 
You can drive and park at Inglis falls if you prefer for a fee but the hike in from Harrison park is a nice trail!
Conditions on the trail were good in July - few muddy/slippery spots but otherwise  in great condition with lots of signage!
Free parking at the arboretum. Beautiful trail. Worth taking the glacial potholes detour when approaching the falls. The falls are magnificent.

Lovely trail but poorly marked until you get to the Bruce Trail. 
Parking at Harrison park is free and you can access the Inglis Falls by hiking.
Pleasant and Easy Trail through the forest with great views. Muddy in some parts of the trail due to rains. Overall worth it.
Couple of rocky scrambles.
Absolutely stunning Trail well worth the walk.
Worth the e trip!
The trail was beautiful the whole way! We had the best time!
Loved it the snow was beautiful lots of pretty scenery
Beautiful snowy day. Need cleats for trail. Quiet day,didn't see anyone else. But the best view was from parking lot overlooking Inglis Falls. It's a workout thru the snow.
Icy right now
It was wet but pretty today!
A bit muddy but a beautiful hike
Nice relaxing trail with the sound of the river beside you. Inglis falls was amazing!!
Great trail - well marked and easy to pay for parking- walked most of the trail  and the waterfall was amazing
Bit wet a D

Fall colours at their peak on Sept 30th and the salmon were running.  Great view from the falls. Some damp areas even in the fall. Many side trails. It's easy to get lost without knowing the way. Thanks to Alltrails we were able to backtrack when we made mistakes. The part going up or down the escarpment is moderately challenging for us seniors.
Gorgeous
Waterfall is so beautiful. Totally worth the hike. I was here in late summer and it looked like a tropical oasis. Great vistas

Enjoyed the trail. A bit muddy in spots but very pretty along the River. Took approximately two hours return. Some spots along escarpment harder than expected. Inglis Falls was beautiful, well worth the trip
Beautiful trail, but the signage is not great…had to check All Trails twice and double back.
Trail is easy to moderate . There are many spots with really beautiful forest landscape . We enjoy every step on this trail. However don’t forget hiking boots… just in case
It is 8km not 6km but very nice falls to see at the end
Best to go off-trail to avoid crowds and you will be able to get a closer view of the falls, trail can get a tad steep but with good footing and shoes then you’ll get up and down no problem!
Little buggy and crowded- but then its a long weekend. Trails have some more challenging sections but overall a nice stroll. Dogs loved swimming in the river!
Buggy. Lots of roots
If you get off the trail, they can be pretty steep and slippery. But a nice adventure.
Beautiful spot with wonderful scenery and views of the falls.
It's a bug
Really enjoyed this trail; lots of variety in the terrain. Glad I had hiking boots and  poles for the wet slippery parts. Started at Harrison Park to the falls and back.
Beautiful trail.

Nice trail with lots of variation and a beautiful waterfall to reward you at the end. Some steeper sections and some flat with gravel. We missed a turn for one of the side trails and ended up returning the same way we came instead of doing the recommended loop. Watch the trail markers!
A bit muddy in spots but a beautiful trail.
Combination of flat, rocky and steep inclines. Ground was totally dry. Perfect day to hike & the falls are beautiful right now.
Lovely, but steep and icy in parts.
Amazing views on both waterfalls
Great time of year to hike. The leaves are turning and the salmon are running upstream. Mostly an easy trail but there are a few spots that were more moderate. Beautiful view at the falls.
Y. Nb n guys
Waterfall the payoff at the end and then back feels worthy
Beautiful!!
Fabulous
Easy at first. Paced trial in the beginning then it’s moderate from there on out. Inclines and lots of rocks. If it rains be ready for mud!
Very safe trail. Beautiful
The trail is well marked. Not too difficult. Beautiful views!
Went visit on June 25/22  …. Beautiful area but kinda sad that you can’t get closer to falls or see it with better view

definitely moderate
bring good shoes
fun hike
It was great
Lovely trail through forest with parts alongside the river.
nice trail. good condition. they could use better trail markers system.
Lovely medium skill hike with some amazing vistas of the Inglis Mill.
Wish there was a trail to the bottom of the falls.
Very icy and muddy but a beautiful trail
Slippery
No words…picture perfect.
Trails are left covered just watch your step. Beauty day for a hike with my boys
beautiful! lots of roots so be aware

We started at Harrison Park since it's free parking there. The trail can be tricky as some parts were really steep and also on a rocky stone in mud kinda pathway. Overall a great hike, just have to watch your steps.
Family friendly path with some bigger hills that give it just enough of a challenge to make it fun!
very nice trail. We did it after a bunch of rain so it was a little muddy but overall very nice trail to do in the fall
Lovely trail through some gorgeous terrain. After some heavy rainfall, the Falls were rushing and really impressive.
Wonderful fall day

Started off on a paved path in beautiful Harrison Park, soon a gravel trail crossing the Sydenham River twice. This is spawning season for the salmon.  We saw several salmons going up the river.
Part of the trail had some climbs with rocky footing.
At the top of the trail we were rewarded with a spectacular view of the Inglis Falls. 
All in all, a great hike.

It's a nice trail to take from
 Harrison Park to Inglis Falls. There are some areas that are quite rocky and lots of tree roots that got slippery after the rain. I would not consider this an easy trail, although there were some areas that are really easy. I enjoyed the views,  however I think better signs are needed as we had to backtrack and wondered what road to take especially when there are forks on the road. Thankfully we had AllTrails and Google maps open. Inglis Falls is gorgeous.
Great trails, lots of rocks and tree roots!
Do it again 100%
Beautiful falls, however no clear/safe way down to the bottom.
Great trail! Not too busy. Well kept but naturally rough in some areas.

Lots of rocks and roots to climb over, hilly terrain,  beautiful forest and falls.

''The hiking trail begins next to the washroom building.  This 0.8km rigorous trail to the falls is very rigorous and is rated “difficult” – rocky terrain, steep path/cliffs.''

Some areas of the trail were easier to navigate then others.
Park at Harrison Park it is free parking and hike up to the falls
was a great trail and nice parking with lots to do for families.
It was strenuous for a couch goer lol
This is one of my favourite hikes! Beautiful scenery, variety of terrain, well maintained, and many side trails. Fairly easy for all types of hikers and dogs.
Great Hike, slightly more difficult than anticipated. Low traffic with worthwhile views

If parking at falls it’s $10, lots of people! No trail to base of falls, look out at top is on the left side,  majority of trails to the right, nice area to hike lots or roots. So many different options to walk, some marked some not, trails on here don’t appear in real life!
The trail was pretty straight forward, not that difficult. If you're there just to see the Falls there's a place you can just park at and it's right there.
Gorgeous!

Great adventure. There was a lot of climbing. I would not recommend it for families with small kids. Took 2.5 hrs to do there and back, steep and slippery in spots but a great challenge. 
Would rate as a moderate trail.
The trail is pretty and not very challenging but the beginning from Harrison Campground is not well marked.  Follow the red and white markers.

Falls are not accessible to get a good view from the bottom. There are other trails and we took the red one. Beautiful enchanted forest with little people (around 9am). Got lost a few times and had to consult the map.
Trail is excellent for beginners and has some great views. However, not great if you have a young dog who is not used to hiking.  The trails are also not marked well at all, so very easy to get lost.
Hard and easy trails not well marked. Got off of easy trail onto hard trail very easily.
Amazing! Super easy trail!

Loved it! At the start I had to pay $10 to park at Inglis Falls and the waterfall is right at the start (on the left, trail on right). Lots of routes to Harrison Park, quiet trail, loved it! End to end is about 7k!
Great hike. Running shoes are ok but hiking boots would be better if you take the Brice!  The Sydenham river keeps you company for part of the hike!  Different woods it seems on every turn

Enjoyed this trail. It was raining and slick but the trails are well marked and travelled. The only disappointing thing is the waterfalls are at the start of the hike and access able in the parking lot.

Started in Harrison Park and hiked to the falls. One of the best trails I’ve done. Multiple glimpses of water downstream from the falls and Inglis Falls itself is a beautiful view. Was not busy, but could imagine it getting very busy around the falls in the summer.
Absolutely stunning! Not very packed and the falls are looking ferocious.
fantastic hike today. the falls are outstanding and the trail is hard packed.  spectacular views of the falls and the rushing streams
Beautiful
nothing spectacular to mention.. will go again later in the season
Still icy. Bring crampons

Very nice set of trails, the River views were lovely. I did all of the trails and side trails. The only downside was it was very icy and the trails are rather heavily traveled, but this is what happens in such a nice spot.
beautiful trail, no matter which way you go!
It will be nice view in the spring, frozen right now, a nice walk but the view will be more fascinating when water will be running again
Beautiful trail easy to walk beautiful views
Very beautiful after the snowfall, well marked trail. We did not need snowshoes, the snow on the trail was well packed.

Well marked and good alternatives to the main trail.  Some slippery bits due to recent weather.  Plenty of parking options.  Do yourself a favour and make the falls your midway or endpoint...reward is worth it!  Will definitely be back!
Gorgeous trail! The falls are an absolute must see! If you follow the trail up to Harrison’s Park you can also check out Weavers falls!
A beautiful trail, even in November. We did a 6ish km loop starting and finishing at the falls. Trail would be a nice run too.

It's a very nice trail with rocky and mildly hilly terrain. Be careful walking it in autumn as the leaves mostly cover the tree roots making it 100% feasible for one to trip and fall..
mild traffic and very beautiful to walk, dog friendly.
Awesome trail. Me and my friends hiked for 14kms and listened to music the whole way. Most amazing way to enjoy the trail.
Trail is so beautiful in fall

Not bad for the first 3/4, decent Bruce Hike. But then when you get to the end? Hop some fences and scale some slippery rocks and scramble your way down for tons of fun! Be prepared with gloves and good shoes and no fear of jumping over chasms :p

I parked at the falls and then got on the wrong trail... I went on the pine trail which was very simple but got to close to the main roads... could not figure out how to get the base of the falls like the other reviews had mentioned. But it was still a beautiful lookout! Just wish I could have figured out the trail properly. Anndddd stop at the post office on hwy 6 for their pie... AMAZING just like Peg Dunnem stated....

The hike was windy, twisty uphill fun. The falls were outstanding. Fun (and easy) to get lost. The company was the best part. 
Also, a tip no one has mentioned yet: at some point you can go right on the trail marked red and white, or left marked red. Go left. It’s incredibly serene and quiet, with more of an incline but probably less treacherous. Wonderful both ways, though. 
Also, also: Follow Peg Dunnem. She gives the most outstanding reviews I’ve ever read. Practically an All Trails Influencer ;) !!

I want to give a shout out to the person who left a review regarding going left out of the parking lot. Follow that advice!!

And now for my review. There are two things that need to sink in: 1) you can ACTUALLY drive to see the falls 2). DO NOT drive to see the falls because you are better than that!  

This trail. Take it. Love it.  It’s rad. Big moments of pure delight. Fun scrambles....I’m sure there’s some caves tucked in there too...and there are giant mossy rocks everywhere...as well as super cool varieties of fungus, annnnddddd chinook salmon swimming upstream! That’s right. Salmon spawning (oh wow, cool band name! Salmon Spawning!). 

And on your way home buy a pie. Nobody ever mentions this...but there is an adorable pie shack on hwy 6. It’s also the post office. It’s unbelievable and the cutest. And when you’ve hiked 9km, you 100% deserve pie. 

Love to you. Another best day on the trail for me!
unreal trails! lots of terrain for all types of walks.

Really good trail! Went on a Sunday and not too many people on the trail. There are a lot of side trails, so it was a little confusing getting up to the falls, but you'll get there one way or another. And be prepared for some elevation gain. The falls were definitely worth it, and lots of nice spots to stop for a snack.
Very busy place!

We loved this one but we were dumb. Parked at lot and headed to right. Thinking path there would get us down below falls. So followed that path for a good 1-1.5 hrs - then turned back along river (more of a make shift side trail vs main) and followed as far as we could. But didn’t get quite to base of falls. Then hiked back out and up to lot - only to discover on left side of lot was better shot and trail to get down to falls. Great afternoon had by 3 teens and 2 adults
you can park right beside the falls if you just want to see that or there are a few other lots around that you can hike to the falls from...well marked and taken care of
Hike is pretty easy... except about 300 meters climb to the falls. You need good footwear to climb that part ..the rest is pretty flat....the falls are worth the view.
Nice trail. Narrow in a few spots. Nice view of falls at parking lot. Parking $6. Dogs enjoyed the walk too

Very nice short trail.  I went on a weekday so I didn’t encounter too many people.  There were some nicer technical trails off the main trail that were well worth the detour.   The falls alone make it worth the trip.

The waterfalls was beautiful and the trails were marked really well. Lots of little streams and you are able to go down by river. As you go farther down the trail towards the river be careful as some areas the rocks are damp.
Good trail, but can be slippery in places. Some steep climbs too, but maybe they seem worse at my age (64). Inglis Falls is impressive.
Lots of trails easy to hike, lots of shade and gorgeous falls, a definite must see!
Gorgeous falls. And enough trails to kill some time. Definitely worth a look during winter as well
trails are open but access to the falls is closef

Great trail! lots of hills with rough footing, proper foot wear is neccesary! NOT stroller friendly! My self my husband, my 5 year old daughter, my small dog and my 1.5 year old daughter on my back in a carrier were able to complete the trail! Their are alot of different trails threw-out so it's nice to have a map to know the most direct route!
Easy hike a few moderate parts. Nice falls. Started at Harrison Park Restaurant
One of the most beautiful falls I've seen, hiked down into the gorge, great rock formations!
Nice trail! Did not expect the falls to be that high and was very enjoyable.
